title: Finite-poset diagrams of filtered representables have simultaneous filtered realizations
statement: Use the universes, regular cardinals and $\kappa$-filteredness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], coherent functors, nerves, transformations and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the infinity category of small spaces of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Small means in the fixed universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal and $C$ a small quasicategory. Put $\mathcal P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ and $j(c)=\operatorname{Map}_C(-,c)$. Let $A$ be a finite partially ordered set, including possibly the empty one, and $F:N(A)\to\mathcal P(C)$ a coherent diagram. Suppose that for every $a\in A$ there exist a small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory $I_a$, a coherent diagram $p_a:I_a\to C$, and a colimiting cocone $jp_a\to\Delta_{I_a}F(a)$ in $\mathcal P(C)$. Then there exist a small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory $I$, a coherent functor $G:I\to\operatorname{Fun}(N(A),C)$ and a coherent cocone $j_*G\to\Delta_I F$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(N(A),\mathcal P(C))$, where $j_*$ is postcomposition with $j$, such that evaluation at every $a\in A$ gives a colimiting cocone $i\mapsto j(G(i)(a))\to F(a)$ in $\mathcal P(C)$. Thus the same filtered index realizes all arrows and higher simplices of $F$, not only its vertices. No colimits in $C$ are assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, existence/essential-surjectivity assertion, printed pp. 410-411 (PDF pp. 427-428), read online. The finite-poset hypothesis is essential, as explained in Warning 5.3.5.16. No Stacks Project tag states this quasicategorical result; HTT is not archived in literature/.

proof.text: If $A=\varnothing$, take $I=\Delta^0$ and the unique functor to $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,C)$, which is terminal even when $C$ is empty; evaluation requirements are vacuous. Assume henceforth $A\ne\varnothing$. Put $P=\mathcal P(C)$ and let $C_0\subset P$ be the replete full essential image of $j$. Presheaf free cocompletion makes $P$ locally small and cocomplete. Yoneda evaluation and pointwise colimits give $\operatorname{Map}_P(jc,-)\simeq\operatorname{ev}_c$, which preserves all small colimits, also after inclusion into larger-universe spaces. Thus each $jc$ is $\kappa$-compact in $P$. Yoneda is fully faithful, and the full-essential-image theorem supplies a coherent quasi-inverse $h:C_0\to C$ with $jh\simeq1_{C_0}$ and $hj\simeq1_C$. In particular $C_0$ is essentially small. Compactness passes to an equivalent object by precomposing the mapping-space functors with that equivalence, so every object of $C_0$ is $\kappa$-compact in $P$.

source.place: Propositions 5.1.2.2 and 5.1.3.1; compactness argument of Proposition 5.3.5.5, in P rather than Ind; read online, archive WANTED.

proof.text: For $X\in P$ let $R_X=C_0\times_P P_{/X}$, using the join-slice model: its $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to P$ with final vertex $X$ whose initial face lies in $C_0$, and the source projection restricts to that face. By the slice right-fibration theorem $P_{/X}$ is a quasicategory, and $R_X$ is its full simplicial subset on the vertices with source in $C_0$, so every inner horn of $R_X$ fills inside $R_X$; thus $R_X$ is a quasicategory. Apply representable-slice density with $D=C$, $y=j$ and $A=C_0$, the full subcategory of objects equivalent to some $j(c)$ (Step 1); then $A_{/X}$ is exactly $R_X$. It gives that $R_X$ is essentially small and that the canonical cocone $\delta_X:(R_X)^{\triangleright}\to P$, obtained by appending $X$ to the source projection, is colimiting with apex $X$. This is the specified tautological cocone with all its higher simplices, not merely some presentation of $X$ as a colimit of representables; this is the density assertion used below.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.3 and Corollary 5.3.5.4, canonical representable slice and its tautological colimit; read online, archive WANTED.

proof.text: If $X$ has a small $\kappa$-filtered representable presentation, then $R_X$ is $\kappa$-filtered. Reindex that presentation by a small $\kappa$-directed poset using the cofinal-poset theorem in the cocomplete category $P$. A diagram $q:K\to R_X$ with $K$ $\kappa$-small is a source diagram in $C_0$ and a specified coherent cocone to $X$. Apply compact relative cocone factorization in $P$ to this presentation, with $K'=\varnothing$ and all source vertices compact by Step 1. It produces a stage $jc$, a coherent source cocone to $jc$, and its full compatibility with the original cocone to $X$. These are a cocone in $R_X$. The fixed-boundary join/cone comparison, applied in the opposite quasicategory for right cocones, keeps the prescribed diagram $q$; the opposite/cone identifications are those of the relative-cone equivalence theorem. For $K=\varnothing$, choose any stage of the nonempty presentation index, giving $jc\to X$. This verifies the definition of $\kappa$-filteredness including the empty case. In particular every $R_{F(a)}$ is $\kappa$-filtered by the hypotheses of the item. By Step 2 its tautological cocone to $F(a)$ is colimiting in $P$.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, (2) implies (1), expanded using Proposition 5.3.4.16; read online, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Let $D$ be the coherent comma category of diagrams $H:N(A)\to C_0$ with a transformation $H\to F$. The relative-slice theorem identifies it with a section quasicategory and makes it essentially small, since $C_0$ is essentially small, $P$ is locally small and $N(A)$ is small. We use the equivalent join-slice model in $\operatorname{Fun}(N(A),P)$; the join/cone comparison commutes with both the boundary and the source, including fixed-boundary pullbacks. The source projection and tautological transformation define a cocone with apex $F$. Evaluation at $a$ gives a functor $e_a:D\to R_{F(a)}$, with the join and arrow versions identified by that comparison. We prove that $D$ is $\kappa$-filtered and that each $e_a$ is cofinal; this will identify the evaluation of its tautological cocone with the colimit of Step 3.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, definition of D and reduction to (a) and (b); read online, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the poset-cone test to $D$. Let $|B|<\kappa$ and let $N(B)\to D$ be a diagram. In the join model, currying its transformation to $F$ gives $U_0:N(A\times(B\amalg\{\infty'\}))\to P$, where $b<\infty'$ for all $b\in B$, its $\infty'$ row is $F$, and every $B$ row lies in $C_0$. Choose a linear ordering $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $A$ extending its partial order. Adjoin $\infty$ between $B$ and $\infty'$. The induction claim is that there is an extension $U_k$ to the full subposet $Q_k=(A\times(B\amalg\{\infty'\}))\cup(\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\times\{\infty\})$ whose new vertices lie in $C_0$, agreeing exactly with $U_{k-1}$. The base is $U_0$. At $a=a_k$, the lower link of the new vertex $(a,\infty)$ is $M=(A_{\leq a}\times B)\cup(A_{<a}\times\{\infty\})$ and its upper link is $T=A_{\geq a}\times\{\infty'\}$. Every new chain is a chain of $M$, then the new vertex, then a chain of $T$. Consequently the prescribed boundary is exactly a diagram $v:N(M)\to C_{0,/F|_{N(A_{\geq a})}}$, and filling it is exactly a cocone on $v$ in this join slice. This identification is obtained degreewise by concatenating the indicated three chains; all faces and degeneracies preserve the concatenation. The least element of $A_{\geq a}$ is $a$, so initial-poset slice restriction supplies a trivial Kan fibration $r:C_{0,/F|_{N(A_{\geq a})}}\to R_{F(a)}$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, proof (a), construction of Q_k and M; Remark 5.3.1.12 and dual Proposition 2.1.2.5; read online, archive WANTED.

proof.text: The simplicial set $N(M)$ is $\kappa$-small. For $\kappa=\aleph_0$ both $A$ and $B$ are finite, and a nondegenerate chain has bounded length. For uncountable $\kappa$, $|M|<\kappa$ and its finite chains form a union over countably many lengths of sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$; regularity gives the bound. By Step 3, $R_{F(a)}$ is $\kappa$-filtered, so $rv$ has a cocone on $N(M)^{\triangleright}$. Lift it through $r$, fixing $N(M)$, using the arbitrary-boundary clause of initial-poset slice restriction. Its cone vertex has source in $C_0$, and the chain identification in Step 5 gives exactly $U_k$. This proves the induction. For $B=\varnothing$ the same argument starts with empty lower link at the first vertex and uses nonemptiness of $R_{F(a_1)}$. At $k=n$ the row at $\infty$ and its transformations from the $B$ rows, with their compatibility to $F$, give a cocone on the original diagram $N(B)\to D$. The poset-cone test proves that $D$ is $\kappa$-filtered.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, proof (a), completion of the vertex insertion induction; read online, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $a\in A$ and $d=(R\to F(a))\in R_{F(a)}$. Put $E=(d\downarrow e_a)$, with objects $(H\to F,d\to H(a))$ and all coherent triangles. By space-transport classification it is the pullback along $e_a$ of the source-fixed arrow left fibration over $R_{F(a)}$ classified by $\operatorname{Map}(d,-)$. Pullback preserves the stated horn-lifting properties degreewise. An inner horn in $E$ is filled by first filling its projection in the quasicategory $D$ and then lifting through this left fibration. Thus $E$ is a quasicategory. The categories $D$ and $R_{F(a)}$ are essentially small by Steps 2 and 4, hence locally small. On small representatives the classifier has small space values; the small-representative clause of space-transport classification makes its total space small. Consequently $E$ is essentially small.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, proof (b), printed p.411 (PDF p.428), local relative version of the vertex insertion in proof (a). The source calls the comma argument a minor variation; this statement makes its distinguished-vertex extension precise. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Apply the poset-cone test to $E$. Given $N(B)\to E$ with $|B|<\kappa$, use the join/cone comparison, first for the transformation to $F$ and then for the fixed-source comma data in $R_{F(a)}$. Its fixed-boundary and product base-change clauses let us work with the following joint data: the diagram $U_0$ of Step 5 and a map $\beta:N(B^{\triangleleft})\to R_{F(a)}$ with initial value $d$, whose $B$ boundary is the evaluation at $a$ of $U_0$. This includes the specified triangles to $F(a)$, not only arrows in the homotopy category. A joint extension to $B^{\triangleright}$ gives a cocone in this join model of $E$. To obtain a cocone on the original diagram, apply a coherent inverse comparison and compose its legs with the unit equivalence on that diagram. Functor/cone calculus supplies the coherent composition and equivalence data. Thus it suffices to construct the joint extension with its boundary fixed.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, proof (b), printed p.411 (PDF p.428), local relative version of the vertex insertion in proof (a). The source calls the comma argument a minor variation; this statement makes its distinguished-vertex extension precise. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Choose the same linear extension $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $A$ as in Step 5. For every vertex preceding $a$, perform exactly the ordinary lower-link insertion of Steps 5-6: choose a cocone in $R_{F(a_k)}$ and lift it through the least-vertex restriction with the entire lower-link boundary fixed. The $a$ row has not changed, so its prescribed map $\beta$ remains fixed. At $a$, apply relative vertex insertion with $\mathcal E=P$, $\mathcal E_0=C_0$, $L=\{a_k:a_k\text{ precedes }a\}$, and the just constructed $U$. This $L$ is an order ideal and $a$ is minimal in its complement. The node's filteredness hypothesis is Step 3 for $R_{F(a)}$; all nonfinal-row vertices of $U$ lie in $C_0$. The result is the next extension $U'$ and a map $\beta':N((B^{\triangleright})^{\triangleleft})\to R_{F(a)}$ restricting to $\beta$ and to the new $a$ row. In particular the new row object has an arrow from $d$ with the entire prescribed family of triangles and higher simplices.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, proof (b), printed p.411 (PDF p.428), local relative version of the vertex insertion in proof (a). The source calls the comma argument a minor variation; this statement makes its distinguished-vertex extension precise. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: For each remaining vertex $a_k$, use the ordinary insertion of Steps 5-6 with lower link $M_k=(A_{\leq a_k}\times B)\cup(A_{<a_k}\times\{\infty\})$ and tail $A_{\geq a_k}$. Step 3 supplies filteredness at $F(a_k)$; the chain count of Step 6 makes $N(M_k)$ $\kappa$-small. Least-vertex slice restriction lifts the chosen cocone while fixing the whole existing diagram. Hence the already completed $a$ row stays exactly fixed, and the previously obtained $\beta'$ stays fixed as a map to $R_{F(a)}$. At the last vertex, the completed $U_n$ and this same $\beta'$ are the joint extension required in Step 8. They give a cocone in $E$ on the original diagram, including all its comma triangles, by that step's comparison. For $B=\varnothing$, relative vertex insertion still supplies the edge from $d$, so it supplies an object of $E$ as well. The poset-cone test proves that $E$ is $\kappa$-filtered.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, proof (b), printed p.411 (PDF p.428), local relative version of the vertex insertion in proof (a). The source calls the comma argument a minor variation; this statement makes its distinguished-vertex extension precise. Read online; archive WANTED. proof.text: Choose small representatives for $D$, $R_{F(a)}$ and each comma category when invoking the small-index cofinality statements. A small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory is weakly contractible by the coslice-colimit theorem. Steps 7-10 therefore makes every comma $(d\downarrow e_a)$ weakly contractible. The coherent cofinal-comma criterion shows that restriction along $e_a$ preserves and detects colimiting cocones, with the same vertex and the specified legs. Apply it to the tautological source diagram $R_{F(a)}\to P$, whose cocone to $F(a)$ is colimiting by Steps 2-3. Its restriction is precisely evaluation at $a$ of the source cocone on $D$. Hence every evaluation of that cocone is colimiting. The pointwise-colimit criterion then says that the cocone on $D\to\operatorname{Fun}(N(A),P)$ itself is colimiting with apex $F$. No colimit is formed in $C$ or $C_0$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, proof (b), Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Lemma 5.3.1.20; read online, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a small quasicategory $I$ and an equivalence $u:I\to D$, with coherent inverse $v:D\to I$ and unit $\eta:1_I\simeq vu$. For a $\kappa$-small simplicial set $K$ and diagram $q:K\to I$, filteredness of $D$ gives a cocone on $uq$. Applying $v$ gives a cocone on $vuq$; precomposing its legs with $\eta q$ gives a coherent cocone on the original diagram $q$. Thus $I$ is $\kappa$-filtered. Write $S:D\to\operatorname{Fun}(N(A),C_0)$ for the source functor. Restrict the tautological cocone along $u$, giving its specified apex $F$ and source $Su$. For each testing target, restriction along $u$ induces an equivalence of cocone spaces: reindexing along $v$ and whiskering with the unit and counit give an inverse. The mapping-space colimit criterion therefore shows that this reindexed cocone and each of its evaluations remain colimiting. Compose the source functor $I\to\operatorname{Fun}(N(A),C_0)$ with postcomposition by the quasi-inverse $h:C_0\to C$ from Step 1. This defines $G:I\to\operatorname{Fun}(N(A),C)$. The coherent natural equivalence $jh\simeq1_{C_0}$, whiskered with the source functor, composes with the tautological transformation to give $j_*G\to\Delta_I F$. Its evaluation cocones differ from those of Step 11 by this natural equivalence. Mapping-space equivalences and the colimit criterion show that they remain colimiting, with their prescribed apex $F(a)$. This constructs the same filtered index, all arrows and all higher compatibility simplices required in the statement.
